1.s: “Yahweh is a jealous God and avenges.” He is slow to anger and great in power; “Yahweh is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble.” Good news: Nineveh’s yoke will be broken.
1.d: Nahum means “comfort”: God will encourage his people through Nineveh’s fall [[tosn:Nahum 1:1]]. God’s vengeance is never random but flows from his holiness, justice and faithfulness [[tosn:Nahum 1:2]]. The messenger bringing peace (1:15) echoes Isaiah 52:7 [[tosn:Nahum 1:15]].

2.s: A vivid description of the attack on Nineveh: chariots racing in the streets, the city plundered.
2.d: Nineveh’s walls and forces could not save it [[tosn:Nahum 2:1]]. A coalition of Babylonians, Medes and Scythians took the city after a three-month siege in 612 BC, a date confirmed by a Babylonian chronicle [[tbd:002:Book of Nahum]].

3.s: “Woe to the bloody city!” Nineveh will fall like ripe figs into the mouth of the eater, and all who hear will clap their hands.
3.d: Assyrian cruelty is well documented [[tosn:Nahum 3:1]]. Thebes, Egypt’s great capital, had fallen to Assyria around 663 BC [[tbd:002:Book of Nahum]] [[tosn:Nahum 3:8]]. God was patient with Nineveh in Jonah’s day, but the Assyrians returned to cruelty [[tosn:Nahum 3:19]].
